mainTopic: קידוש בבית הכנסת and קידוש במקום סעודה: the views of רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן
overview: This amud continues the מחלוקת about people who hear קידוש in the בית הכנסת. רב holds they fulfill קידוש, and שמואל holds they do not. The גמרא explains why each side still keeps the familiar practice. For רב, the home קידוש is for the family. For שמואל, the shul קידוש is for guests who eat there. שמואל's view comes from his rule אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה, and רב ענן בר תחליפא shows that this rule applies even when moving within one house. רב הונא and רבה are shown to follow the same rule. The גמרא then explains why רבה's practice does not contradict אביי's report that he usually followed רב: he followed רב's stringencies but not his leniencies. Finally, רבי יוחנן says that shul קידוש even covers the wine ברכה. The גמרא begins showing that this fits his ruling on changing wine, a quote that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל: those who hear קידוש in shul do not fulfill it
steps.stepSummary: The end of שמואל's position: people who hear קידוש in the בית הכנסת have not fulfilled even the קידוש obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the obligation of קידוש they have not fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of שמואל's side of the argument. He says that hearing קידוש in shul does not count at all, so a person must make קידוש again at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had said that people in shul do fulfill the קידוש obligation. שמואל goes further with the word אף ('even'). In his view nothing is accomplished for them, not even קידוש itself. This sets up the two questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing that sanctifies שבת or יום טוב, said over wine
Even (signals going further than the other opinion)

phrases.english: Even the obligation of kiddush they have not fulfilled.
phrases.notes: שמואל's statement, completing the מחלוקת with רב that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the מחלוקת between רב and שמואל that began on the previous lines of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, hearing קידוש in the בית הכנסת does not fulfill the קידוש obligation.

steps.title: Question on רב: why make קידוש again at home?
steps.stepSummary: If רב holds that קידוש in shul counts, why do people repeat קידוש at home?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב, why does he need to make קידוש in his house?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's view using the common practice of making קידוש again at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person already fulfilled קידוש in shul, a second קידוש at home looks unnecessary. It could even look like a ברכה לבטלה (a wasted blessing). So the familiar practice seems to contradict רב.

phrases.english: But according to Rav,
why does he need to make kiddush in his house?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב, לְמָה לֵיהּ לְקַדּוֹשֵׁי בְּבֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to examine רב's side of the מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that קידוש in shul fulfills the obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the obligation is already fulfilled, the accepted practice of repeating קידוש at home seems pointless.

steps.title: Answer: to fulfill the obligation for his family
steps.stepSummary: The home קידוש is for his children and household, who were not in shul.
steps.simpleTranslation: In order to fulfill the obligation for his children and the members of his household.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. The second קידוש is not for the man himself but for his family at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family did not hear קידוש in shul, so they still need it. The man who already fulfilled his own obligation can still recite it for them. The practice therefore fits רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill an obligation on behalf of others

phrases.english: In order to fulfill the obligation of
his children and the members of his household.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the purpose: the home קידוש is for other people, not for the man himself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating קידוש at home shows that the shul קידוש did not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The home קידוש exists for the family, so רב's view stands.

steps.title: Question on שמואל: why make קידוש in shul at all?
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל holds that shul קידוש accomplishes nothing, why is it said there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, why do I need to make קידוש in the בית הכנסת?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the other side. If shul קידוש helps no one, why do we say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the question on רב. For רב the home קידוש looked unnecessary. For שמואל the shul קידוש looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel,
why do I need to make kiddush in the synagogue?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, לְמָה לִי לְקַדּוֹשֵׁי בְּבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel challenge, now aimed at שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that shul קידוש fulfills nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no one fulfills anything, the established practice of קידוש in shul seems pointless.

steps.title: Answer: for guests who eat and sleep in the shul
steps.stepSummary: Shul קידוש is for guests who eat their meal in the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: To fulfill the obligation of guests, who eat, drink, and sleep in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. Shul קידוש serves travelers who actually eat their שבת meal there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these guests the shul is the place of their meal, so the קידוש counts for them. For everyone else, who goes home to eat, it does not count. This answer prepares the next step, which shows that the meal's location is the key factor for שמואל.

phrases.english: To fulfill the obligation of guests,
who eat and drink
and sleep in the synagogue.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the practice to a specific group of people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shul קידוש is for the whole congregation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shul קידוש is for guests who eat there, which is consistent with שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: קידוש only where the meal is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that שמואל's view follows his general principle, אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning, as שמואל said: There is no קידוש except in the place of the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the root of שמואל's opinion. קידוש only counts if you eat your meal in the same place where you heard it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains both earlier points. People who go home to eat did not fulfill קידוש in shul. Guests who eat in shul did. The location of the meal decides everything.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (consistent with his other statement)
In the place of the meal

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule is אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה: קידוש counts only where the meal is eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: קידוש במקום סעודה became accepted הלכה. One must eat in the place where one hears קידוש.

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said:
There is no kiddush except in the place of the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds שמואל's position and his answer in his broader principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידוש is valid only in the place where the meal is eaten.

steps.title: The students' assumption: the rule applies only between houses
steps.stepSummary: The students assumed that moving within the same house is not considered changing places.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from it: This applies only from house to house, but from place to place within one house — no.
steps.whatsHappening: The students make a guess about how far שמואל's rule reaches. This step sets up the next move, where the guess will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students limit 'place of the meal' to the whole house. On their reading, only going to a different house breaks the connection between קידוש and the meal. Moving between rooms or floors of one house would not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (an assumption that is often later rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: סבור מינה signals an assumption, not a conclusion. Do not treat this as the הלכה. It is about to be rejected.

phrases.english: They understood from it:
This applies only from house to house,
but from place to place
within one house — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the scope of שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed reading: only moving to another house counts as changing places.

steps.title: רב ענן בר תחליפא: שמואל repeated קידוש within one house
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן בר תחליפא testifies that שמואל went down from the roof and made קידוש again. So even a move within one house counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן בר תחליפא said to them: Many times I stood before שמואל, and he went down from the roof to the ground and made קידוש again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן בר תחליפא rejects the students' assumption. He reports from what he saw that שמואל made קידוש again after moving within the same house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going from the roof to the ground floor is a move inside one house. Even so, שמואל repeated קידוש. This proves that changing places within one house also breaks the link between קידוש and the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing before him (serving or learning from him)

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, even moving from one part of a house to another (roof to ground floor) requires a new קידוש.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב עָנָן בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא:
phrases.english: Rav Anan bar Tachlifa said to them:
Many times
I was standing before Shmuel,
and he went down from the roof to the ground
and made kiddush again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב עָנָן בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the students' assumption from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed limit that the rule applies only from house to house
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל's own practice shows that a move within one house also requires a new קידוש.
steps.raayaObject: Even a change of place within one house counts for קידוש במקום סעודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Eyewitness report of שמואל's practice (מעשה רב).

steps.title: רב הונא also requires קידוש where the meal is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב הונא also held אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה. When his lamp went out after קידוש, he moved to his son רבה's house, made קידוש again, and ate there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא also holds that קידוש counts only in the place of the meal. Once רב הונא made קידוש and his lamp went out. His things were brought to the wedding house of his son רבה, where there was a lamp. There he made קידוש again and tasted some food. So we see he holds that קידוש counts only in the place of the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another אמורא, רב הונא, who agrees with שמואל's rule. It proves this from something רב הונא actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא had already made קידוש, but his lamp went out, so he could not eat there. He moved to a new house to eat and said קידוש again. That shows he held his first קידוש did not count, because he did not eat where he made it.

keyTerms.meaning: Was uprooted, meaning it went out
So we see / apparently (introduces a conclusion drawn from facts)

steps.confusionAlert: The second קידוש was not caused by the dark lamp or by the move as such. It was needed because רב הונא ate his meal somewhere other than where he made the first קידוש. Had he already eaten in the first place, the move would not have mattered. קידוש has to be tied to the meal.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna also holds
there is no kiddush except in the place of the meal.
For Rav Huna made kiddush,
and his lamp went out,
phrases.notes: Without light he could not eat his meal there.

phrases.english: and his belongings were brought
to the wedding house of Rabba his son
where there was a lamp
and he made kiddush and tasted something,
so apparently he holds:
there is no kiddush except in the place of the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב הוּנָא סָבַר אֵין קִידּוּשׁ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם סְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second אמורא who agrees with שמואל's general rule from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא also holds that קידוש must be made where the meal is eaten. This is proven from his conduct when his lamp went out.

steps.title: רבה also requires קידוש where the meal is eaten
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that רבה told his students to eat something after his קידוש. Their own lodging's lamp might go out, and the קידוש they heard from him would not count unless they ate where they heard it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה also holds that קידוש counts only in the place of the meal. אביי said: When I was at my teacher's house, whenever he made קידוש he told us, 'Taste something. Maybe by the time you reach your lodging, your lamp will have gone out. Then you will not be able to make קידוש where you eat. And you will not fulfill your duty with the קידוש here, since קידוש counts only in the place of the meal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third אמורא, רבה, who also follows this rule. The proof is what אביי heard him say to his students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה worried that his students might arrive home to a dark room and be unable to eat or make קידוש there. So he had them eat a little right away. That way the קידוש they heard from him would be attached to a meal and would count.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of my master (אביי's name for his teacher רבה)
You fulfill your obligation (literally: you go out)

phrases.english: And Rabba also holds
there is no kiddush except in the place of the meal.
For Abaye said:
When I was at my master's house,
when he would make kiddush he would say to us:
Taste something,
perhaps by the time you go to your lodging
your lamp will go out
and you will not make kiddush in the place of eating,
and with the kiddush here you do not fulfill your obligation,
since there is no kiddush except in the place of the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבָּה סָבַר אֵין קִידּוּשׁ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם סְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 9. It adds רבה to the list of those who follow the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה holds that קידוש counts only where the meal is eaten. He told his students to eat right away so his קידוש would count for them.

steps.title: Challenge: אביי said רבה followed רב except in three cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבה could follow שמואל's rule here. אביי himself said that רבה always followed רב except in three listed cases, and this rule is not one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But אביי said: In everything, my master acted like רב, except for these three, where he acted like שמואל. (1) One may move ציצית strings from one garment to another. (2) One may light from one חנוכה lamp to another. (3) The הלכה follows רבי שמעון about dragging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 10. If רבה always followed רב except in three specific cases, how could he follow שמואל's rule about קידוש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה is שמואל's approach (Step 6). אביי's list says רבה sided with שמואל only three times, and קידוש is not on that list. So either the list is incomplete, or our claim about רבה is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (an expression of surprise that opens a challenge)
One may untie ציצית from one garment and move them to another
One may light one חנוכה lamp from another

steps.confusionAlert: The three cases on the list have nothing to do with קידוש. That is exactly the point. The challenge is that קידוש is missing from a list that claims to be complete.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Abaye say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִילֵּי דְּמָר הֲוָה עָבֵיד כְּרַב,
phrases.english: In all matters, my master would act like Rav,
except for these three, in which he acted like Shmuel:
One may untie tzitzit from garment to garment.
And one may light from lamp to lamp.
And the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon regarding dragging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 10's claim that רבה followed the rule אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 10 that רבה held אין קידוש אלא במקום סעודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's list says רבה followed שמואל in only three cases. קידוש במקום סעודה is not among them, so רבה should have followed רב here.

steps.title: The source for רבי שמעון's ruling on dragging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא behind the third item on אביי's list. רבי שמעון permits dragging furniture on שבת as long as one does not intend to make a groove.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says, a person may drag a bed, a chair, or a bench on שבת, as long as he does not intend to make a groove in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the third item on אביי's list by quoting its source. The answer to the challenge from Step 11 has not come yet. It comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dragging heavy furniture might dig a groove in the ground, which could be a forbidden מלאכה. רבי שמעון permits it because the person does not intend to dig. An unintended result is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A groove or furrow in the ground
Provided that he does not intend

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis of רבי שמעון's well-known principle of דבר שאין מתכוין: an unintended result does not make an action forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹרֵר אָדָם מִטָּה כִּסֵּא וְסַפְסָל בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A person may drag a bed, chair, or bench on Shabbat,
provided that he does not intend to make a groove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third item (גרירה) on אביי's list from Step 11. The challenge itself is answered in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון permits dragging furniture on שבת if there is no intent to make a groove.

steps.title: רבה followed רב's stringencies but not his leniencies
steps.stepSummary: רבה followed רב only when רב was stricter. Here רב was the lenient one, so רבה followed the stricter view of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He acted according to רב's stringencies, but he did not act according to רב's leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11. רבה only followed רב when רב was strict, so here he could follow שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the three cases on אביי's list, שמואל was lenient and רבה followed him. That was the 'exception' to following רב. In the case of קידוש, רב is the lenient one, because he holds that קידוש counts even without eating there. So following שמואל here is just being strict, and that is fully consistent with רבה's approach.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's list of three only covers cases where רבה left רב to be lenient. Leaving רב in order to be strict was not counted, so רבה's קידוש practice does not contradict אביי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה had a fourth exception to following רב. Being strict like שמואל is not considered leaving רב at all.

phrases.english: According to Rav's stringencies he would act,
according to Rav's leniencies he would not act.
phrases.notes: Here רב is lenient (קידוש counts without a meal), so רבה was strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 11 after the side-quote in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the contradicting statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה followed רב in everything except the three listed cases, so following שמואל on קידוש looks like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three cases were leniencies against רב. רבה always accepted רב's stringencies anyway, and here following שמואל is a stringency.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: קידוש in the synagogue even covers the blessing on wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that people who hear קידוש in the בית הכנסת have also fulfilled the ברכה on the wine they will drink at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: they have even fulfilled their obligation for the wine as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original question about people who make קידוש in the בית הכנסת. It adds a third opinion, from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב said they fulfilled קידוש but must say בורא פרי הגפן again at home. שמואל said they did not even fulfill קידוש. רבי יוחנן goes further than רב: the wine ברכה also counts. Since they plan to drink wine at their meal at home, their attention never left the ברכה, so no new ברכה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: the obligation of the ברכה over wine

steps.whyThisMatters: Now there are three views: שמואל (nothing counts), רב (קידוש counts but not the wine ברכה), and רבי יוחנן (both count).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
they have also fulfilled even the obligation of wine.
phrases.notes: They do not need to repeat בורא פרי הגפן at home.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף יְדֵי יַיִן נָמֵי יָצְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבה and returns to the main מחלוקת about קידוש in the בית הכנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who hear קידוש in the בית הכנסת have fulfilled both קידוש and the ברכה on wine. They do not repeat it at home.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning: introducing his rule on changing wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן's view fits his known position, and begins quoting a chain of tradition about changing wine during a meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, as רבי חנין בר אביי said that רבי פדת said that רבי יוחנן said: both a change of wine...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It begins quoting another statement of רבי יוחנן that will show the same thinking. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase ואזדא לטעמיה tells us this ruling is not a one-time idea. It fits a general rule רבי יוחנן holds elsewhere. That rule starts with the case of switching to a new wine during a meal. The full comparison will only become clear once the quote is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: and he follows his own (consistent) reasoning
a change of wine (switching to a different wine)
both / whether (introducing a list of equal cases)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
as Rabbi Chanin bar Abaye said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי פְּדָת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Pedat said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both a change of wine,
